Budget and source reconciliation · Why this platform differs from the earlier Education briefing

The older illustrated Education briefing used different D1–D3 labels and a proposed $480K / $248K estimate. This edition follows the current main DBMI operating plan’s D1–D3 initiative register, first-year windows, M1–M18 delivery gates, and P50 economic cost lines over the 36-month scenario. Older infographic estimates are not treated as approved budgets.

Delivery dependency: D1 is shown in first-year release months 4–6 even though its modeled redeployed-time cost window begins in month 7. D2 has an exploratory release window at months 10–12 but modeled effort begins in month 13. These are sequencing assumptions requiring staff-capacity and authorization review—not evidence of funded rollout.

Three connected initiatives

Click a card for the detailed playbook

One Harvard · coordinated, not centralized

Faculty and learners

Academic authority stays academic

Program directors, faculty mentors, departmental education administrators, and university degree-granting bodies retain their respective responsibilities. The proposed platform coordinates status, handoffs, and evidence.

Industry and translation

OTD keeps agreement authority

DBMI can triage inquiries and connect faculty collaborators. OTD structures intellectual-property, publication, confidentiality, and industry-sponsored research terms. A meeting is not a signed partnership.

Outreach and accountability

Publish what is cleared

Communications assembles a source-verified departmental impact portfolio. Faculty and the responsible HMS offices validate claims and approve release. Draft stories are not verified impact outcomes.

S · Specific

Three initiatives; defined ownership and boundaries

One master program, not three new strategic programs. Each initiative has a deliverable, accountable coordinator, institutional dependencies, and a measurable acceptance test.

Published program and collaboration context

Source-confirmed facts · not additional initiatives or budget
D1 · Education operations · Published

AIM, Dunleavy Fellows and funded pathways

The $6 million Dunleavy Fund for Clinical AI (November 2024) supports AIM PhD Fellows and educational pipeline activities, including planned undergraduate hackathon and research-internship opportunities. The AIM PhD track, co-directed by Zak Kohane and Sebastian Schneeweiss, uses co-mentorship and common datasets; capture distinct mentor roles without presuming an identical pair for every trainee.

MMSc-BMI offers the INDECS Scholarship, covering tuition and mandatory fees over the typical four semesters, subject to award eligibility and satisfactory academic progress.

D1/D3 · Summer institute · Published

SIBMI's documented legacy

The Dr. Susanne E. Churchill Summer Institute in Biomedical Informatics is a nine-week program, renamed in 2024 at its twentieth anniversary. The official FAQ restricts applicants to US citizens or permanent residents. The proposed 2026 session dates should be verified with the program office before public reuse; public program facts do not substitute for individual trainee records.

D2 · Industry collaboration · Published Harvard precedent

XBridge and OTD governance

Harvard–BioMed X XBridge launched a time-limited pilot in January 2026 to match research interests and facilitate scientific discussions. Its assessment categories include fit, industry engagement, discussions, and OTD-executed sponsored research agreements. These are useful reference categories for D2's proposed register, not evidence that DBMI currently participates in the pilot.

One Harvard handoff: use shared intake and source labels while preserving authorized academic, fiscal, data-security, and agreement decisions in their existing offices. No shadow student system, contract authority, or new faculty approval committee is proposed.
M · Measurable

Evidence before targets

Gate 1 establishes denominators and baseline definitions. These are proposed measurement specifications, not reported DBMI results.

InitiativeProposed metricCalculation / evidenceBaselineOwner
Master KPI retained: “Trainee experience — program survey score; time to degree (↑ / ↓)” belongs to D1. Do not combine program cohorts, published HMS statistics, or synthetic workshop records into an unqualified DBMI total.
A · Attainable

Existing offices, documented dependencies, manageable releases

This is a coordination model for a decentralized academic environment, not a request to establish new institutional authority.

Capacity constraints

  • Education program staff need time to define the data dictionary, verify Dunleavy/INDECS funded-cohort fields and AIM co-mentorship roles, and review authorized records.
  • OTD must be consulted early; negotiation and contracting are not fixed DBMI delivery times.
  • Communications depends on faculty approvals, images and permissions, and verified outcomes.
  • D2 has no modeled first-year cost allocation; scope any exploratory work separately before commitment.
  • D1 first-release window (M4–6) precedes its modeled redeployment cost window (M7–18). Agree staff time and access at a gate before treating a prototype as authorized work.

What is not being promised

  • No new degree program, invented enrollment count, or guaranteed placement result.
  • No industry contract, license, or revenue without OTD and relevant institutional approvals.
  • No automated thesis or faculty judgments made by AI.
  • No claim that full D2 and D3 capability is complete by Month 12.
R · Relevant

One Harvard and BEACON alignment

The strategic connections below are the author's proposed alignment, not an HMS endorsement or a live interface to School systems.

Excellence in Academics & Education

Primary for D1: curriculum coordination, trainee experience, appropriate support throughout admission, research training, and completion.

Outcomes & Translation

Primary for D2: preserve academic freedom while expanding the pathway from faculty ideas to legitimate OTD-coordinated collaboration.

Belonging · Collaborative & Transformative Science

Supporting alignments: cross-lab mentoring, alumni relationships, transparent departmental storytelling, and inclusive access to educational opportunities.

T · Time-bound

Three clocks, not one deadline

Clock 1First-year releases · M1–M12Clock 2Portfolio gates · M3–M18Clock 336-month cost and sustained capability spans

The master model starts at January 2027 by default (editable in the master). Months in this standalone demonstration are relative to that assumed start, not approved institutional deadlines.

Three clocks: First-year release windows represent proposed early outputs; M1–M18 gates govern authorization and review; the 36-month cost scenario covers sustained economic effort. D1 (M4–6) and D2 (M10–12) early-release windows precede modeled cost start (M7 and M13). Secure capacity, information access and approvals before executing those steps.

Initiative work windows

Color bars = original economic spans · pale bars = first-year release windows

Six common master-plan decision gates

A gate authorizes the next step only when dependencies and evidence are satisfied; it does not guarantee agreement execution, learner outcomes, or School approval. D2 continues beyond the M18 review to M24; D3 continues to M30 under the economic work spans.
E · Evaluate

Verify evidence and reduce reporting risk

A senior reviewer should be able to answer each test without relying on fictional data, unsupported improvement percentages, or a workshop demonstration.

Financial stewardship · P50 economic scenario

Budget aligned to the master’s actual cost lines

This is a frozen, reproducible snapshot of the master model's defaults, not a second independently estimated budget. Amounts are USD thousands; totals include redeployed staff effort (economic cost) and distinguish new cash.

Cost by initiative and nature

Initiative / modeled lineKindSource model rate / itemP50 cost ($K)Economic timing
Model assumptions (from main platform): median occupational pay, 3.2% annual escalation for 1.5 years, 45.3% fringe on staff time, PERT (optimistic + 4×most-likely + pessimistic)/6, and 10% reserve on incremental cash when included in funding request. D1/D2 are redeployed effort; D3 has the only incremental non-labor line. P50 is a scenario name, not a probability that the project will succeed.
Timing rule: D2 begins at economic Month 13 and has $0 allocation within Year 1 under the main cost schedule. Any first-year exploratory activity needs owner/capacity validation; this platform does not invent a Year-1 D2 budget. Changes to master assumptions do not automatically synchronize this standalone static snapshot.
